# Bounded source-only observation contract

Protocol: `oxid-array-source-typing-observation-v1`. A versioned inert observation object or JSONL stream is acceptable through an independently reviewed lossless mapping. This document fixes semantic fields, order and completeness, not Rust struct spelling. The adapter must be reviewed before candidate observation. Inputs are original source files, explicit `single` or `project` scope, and downward-only resource/observation limits. Fixed observation categories may be requested, never case-specific expected values, supplied origins, ASTs, HIR IDs, type descriptors or callbacks.

The ordinary loader, lossless tape, candidate parser, provenance validation, declaration index and whole-project selector run once. Then the private owned resolve/type seam selects immutable `ObserveArrayTypes` admission internally. All ordinary executable entries retain their old policy and first-feature rejection. Scalar-selected guard sources explicitly report `private-owned-test-seam`; they must also report the actual scalar selector and cannot claim the production selector chose owned.

No resolved/typed object, typed function view, callback, raw parts, raw program, witness, lowering plan or executable artifact escapes. The normal observer never invokes count, lower, source association, ownership, reference/native probes, or execution. Separate local guard tests may call the named guarded entries on successfully typed input; they must fail before output work and return only inert denial/sentinel rows. This does not turn the observer into a raw-verifier bypass.

Required row groups, copied only from actual checked owners:

1. Header: protocol, case identity, selected base, candidate head/tree plus production/adapter digests, explicit scope, requested/actual limits, actual selector per module, actual chosen test path, types-only admission and original root entry identity. Harness case labels identify source inputs; they grant no semantic facts.
2. Source: every original file ID/path/UTF-8 byte length/SHA-256 in ordinary load order, bound to the supplied source bytes. All semantic origins include file/start/end and must validate on that source before text or line/column rendering. Source roles, including root versus child, are explicit.
3. Phase: attempted/completed status for load/lex/parse/provenance/index/select/resolve/type. Resolution completion certifies all record fields, all signatures/local annotations, exposure and all bodies in their existing order. Any resolution failure forbids a type-start marker and all type rows. Type errors may coexist with complete copied resolution rows, but never a typed-success marker or an exported partial typed inventory.
4. Declaration/signature: actual module-major DefId/RecordId, declaration-name origin, function order, original-root entry, parameter positions and ParameterTy modes, result ValueTy. Nominal identity retains real RecordId and declaration origin; fixed arrays carry exact scalar tag/length and have no nominal rows. Signature origin is the existing function-name span, not its entire textual signature.
5. Function/binding/block: actual function ID, binding IDs in allocation order, declaration origin, annotation, mutability, parameter position, scope block ID, body/end origins, and block/statement membership/order. Binding types are actual ParameterTy; references retain shared/exclusive mode.
6. HIR expression: every retained function-local ExprId in append-ID order, kind, complete origin, scalar constant when applicable and every ordered child ID. ArrayLiteral has complete element IDs; IndexRead has actual BindingId, base origin and index ID; ArrayLength has BindingId/base origin. Existing Group, Call, Binding, arithmetic and other encountered scalar/record kinds keep complete original semantics. A Call carries actual target DefId plus declaration origin and ordered value/borrow arguments. No sorting by source span is permitted as a replacement for ID order.
7. Statement: actual function/block/statement position, kind, full origin and all retained origins. IndexAssign contains BindingId/base origin, full target, operator, value ID, index ID and ordered roots `[value,index]`. No Expr row exists for its target wrapper. Existing Let, Return, Assign and FieldAssign preserve their prior root semantics; a source span cannot substitute for a real child ID.
8. Type inventory, only after successful type checking: one nonoptional ValueTy slot for every retained HIR expression ID, including seeded empty leaves and all Groups; one ParameterTy slot per binding; actual unchanged projection facts for record accesses and actual block-flow results if retained. Array access descriptors, when exported, are derived from the actual binding type and BindingId and must retain reference mode. These rows are post-hoc inventory, never a runtime trace or proof of ownership permission.
9. Inventory/resources: independently counted AST expression count/target wrappers/E_ast, retained HIR expression count/E_hir, literal request count and ordered exact-N events. Distinguish reserved-but-unfilled requested entries from retained E_hir. Report measured row widths and checked payload/lifetime accounting separately. Broad runs leave generic WorkMeter logs disabled. Small resource controls may retain bounded passive events with a separately justified bound.
10. Diagnostic: every actual diagnostic in phase/function order, exact code/stage/message, original primary, ordered secondary spans/messages, ordered notes, human bytes and JSON-line bytes. File relocation is permitted only as a verified fixture-relative path mapping; preserve source/file identity and all byte/Unicode locations. No candidate output becomes an expected diagnostic.
11. End: complete=true only after every required row has been copied, validated and emitted; outcome is exactly typed-success, diagnostic-complete, or incomplete-observation. Include exact row counts per category, total retained/serialized bytes, diagnostic count, and phase completion. Typed-success requires no diagnostics and every type slot; diagnostic-complete requires a diagnostic list and no typed-success marker. An observation limit/error never receives qualification credit.

Hard per-case ceilings remain 200,000 semantic rows and 16 MiB serialized observation bytes, with checked counters before storage reservation or copy. Every nested child, argument, field, span and slot entry contributes a row; it cannot hide in one huge JSON array. Count header/source/phase/end rows too. Copied strings and arrays must be included in separate checked auxiliary-retained-byte accounting; Vec/String headers, serializer buffer, source/HIR/typing overlap and any duplicate conversion storage are documented. No unbounded infallible push, unbounded log or source-sized text duplication is justified by an eventual output cap. Limit failure produces an explicit incomplete artifact with zero credit, never truncation.

Missing or duplicate IDs, gaps, unknown tags, wrong file/hash/role, bad UTF-8 origins, references to missing rows, wrong order, duplicate/missing type slots, unchecked counters, partial success plus error, absent completion or unexpected extra rows fail closed. The comparison must prove coverage against whole actual vector lengths. Requested category subsets cannot omit facts required by the selected case's authority.
